title: Chronos Lens — keyboard-first magnifier and semantic telemetry for time-series charts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current time-series interactions rely heavily on hover/tooltips and pointer-driven legends. High-density charts and keyboard-only or screen-reader users have poor access to precise context. Hover tooltips are ephemeral, tooltips serialize lots of DOM nodes, and large series counts cause tooltip reflows and janky interactions.

Proposal: Introduce 'Chronos Lens' — a keyboard-first, persistent magnifier overlay that: (1) can be opened and moved via keyboard (focusable control, arrow/vi-style nudging), (2) renders a low-latency zoomed preview using an offscreen canvas to avoid DOM thrash, (3) exposes a concise semantic summary announced to assistive tech (aria-live region) and available via a compact programmatic API for downstream automation, and (4) maps to design tokens so colors/contrast follow theme and low-power modes.

Key behaviors: open/close via keyboard shortcut (Shift+L default, configurable), focus trap inside lens when active, stepwise zoom levels, legend-context toggle (lens shows only selected series or all), and an inline telemetry row that summarizes min/max, median, and latest-value with microcopy. The semantic summary should prioritize short sentences for TTS and provide an optional expanded verbose mode.

Performance constraints: the lens must hydrate without blocking main thread for charts with up to 1,000 series. Approach: use incremental frame sampling, prefix/KV cache reuse, and offscreen canvas compositing. When WebGL/GPU is available, use a simplified shader path; otherwise fall back to batched 2D canvas. Avoid adding heavy DOM for each series — the lens summary should be synthesized from precomputed aggregates delivered by runtime endpoints or local worker.

Design deliverables: Figma frames for lens states (closed, small, large, pinned), keyboard interaction spec, annotated token map (colors, focus ring, high-contrast variants), and copy for aria messages. Dev deliverables: component API contract (Lens props), minimal DOM fallback spec, and a small E2E test harness (keyboard navigation + SR announcements).

Tradeoffs considered: 1) Embedding DOM tooltips gives richer semantics but scales poorly; we choose synthesized summaries plus a single, stable aria-live region to balance a11y and perf. 2) GPU shaders provide best perf but increase complexity for Dedicated/Private builds; we will gate advanced shader path behind capability detection. 3) Keyboard-first UX requires additional focus management complexity; acceptable for accessibility gains.

Metrics: p50 lens open time < 15ms on representative medium instances; memory overhead < 30MB added for 1,000-series charts; screen-reader users report comprehension improvement in user testing (target: 90th percentile task success > 85%).

Rollout plan: prototype in design system storybook, limited canary on internal dashboard, iteration with ENG for runtime aggregates, then staged rollout behind feature flag.

comments: 2026-03-02 — First pass design uploaded to Figma. Need engineering input on data shape for concise summaries. (Ava)
2026-03-04 — ENG review: prefer precomputed aggregates from runtime to avoid main-thread loops. ENG-9812 to expose lightweight aggregate API. (Marcus)

2026-03-06 — Accessibility review: aria-live region should provide brief summary and a 'details' toggle that can be opened with Enter. Avoid verbose automatic announcements during pan/scroll. (Priya, Accessibility)

2026-03-09 — Prototype tested against 1200-series synthetic dataset on staging. Initial open latency 28ms; need to reduce to <15ms — plan: sample rate reduction + offscreen canvas compositing. (Marcus)
2026-03-11 — Design update: added low-power token variants and high-contrast intent. Preparing acceptance criteria and test plan. (Ava)
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard activation: Chronos Lens can be opened, moved, resized, and closed using keyboard only; documented shortcuts in design tokens.
A11y: Screen reader receives a concise semantic summary on open and can request expanded details; aria-live messages vetted by Accessibility team.
Performance: Lens open time (p50) <= 15ms for a dataset of 1,000 series in staging environment using the offscreen canvas path.
Design tokens: All visual styles for the lens (background, focus ring, summary badges) are implemented using design system tokens and have low-power/high-contrast variants.
Dev integration: ENG exposes an aggregate API or worker pipeline per ENG-9812; component uses it when available and falls back gracefully.
E2E tests: Storybook stories and CI tests cover keyboard flows and a11y announcements; PR includes visual spec screenshots and perf benchmark summary.
